title: deletion-proof-streaming-exporter-and-policy-enforcer
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Build a verifiable, region-aware deletion evidence pipeline and operator that automates Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) requests and periodic retention purges, produces exportable proof artifacts for auditors/customers, and integrates with the Console for monitoring and automated attestations.
background: Regulators and enterprise customers require not only that data is deleted according to retention and residency requirements, but also that we can produce cryptographically verifiable evidence and operational proofs on demand. Existing efforts (retention simulator, purge playbooks) have focused on simulation and manual attestations; we need an operational system that automates deletion, verifies success, and records tamper-evident audit artifacts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Deletion Proof Streaming Exporter (DPSE) backed by an append-only evidence stream. Components: (1) Policy Evaluator: DSL that compiles residency + retention rules into targeted deletion plans; (2) Deletion Operator: region-aware operator that executes deletes with retry semantics and emits signed deletion manifests; (3) Verification Pipeline: async job runner that re-checks object-level and index-level manifests and produces periodic verification snapshots (Merkle root + signatures); (4) Exporter & Attestation Bundler: packages manifests, verification logs, and metadata into a customer-ready package and pushes to configured destinations (S3/GCS/enterprise SIEM) or surfaces in Console for download.
technical_design_notes: Evidence model: every delete action emits a DeletionManifest (JSON) with object keys, timestamps (ISO8601), operator-instance id, and SHA-256 of deleted object reference. Manifests are signed with service key and appended to an append-only ledger (Kafka topic + compacted storage).

Verification: periodic verifier consumes ledger, re-hashes current index state and compares Merkle root snapshots. Discrepancies raise alerts and create forensics bundles. Verification results are recorded as signed VerificationSnapshots with backrefs to the manifests they verified.

Operator implementation: Kubernetes Operator for Dedicated/Private that talks to local storage and uses side-channel deletes for on-prem. For Hosted, a serverless job (worker pool) uses tenant-routing policies. All operators must respect region tags for residency and must support dry-run & replay-mode.

Retention policy DSL: rule primitives for residency (region ISO codes), retention windows, tombstone behavior, and exception lists (legal hold). DSL compiles to targeted selectors and a safe-delete plan that marks items for staged deletion (soft-delete -> delayed hard-delete).
Security & keys: evidence stream signing uses a service key stored in KMS/HSM per deployment. Proof bundles include public key fingerprints and KMS audit references for non-repudiation.

Performance: mass purges should be batched with backpressure to avoid SLO violations. Default batch size heuristics will be driven by model of tokenized object sizes and current serving load; DPSE will integrate with Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design/QA): finalize DSL and manifest schema; security review (KMS integration).
Phase 1 (Canary): deploy operator in staging for a subset of low-traffic tenants; enable dry-run and compare to existing purge playbook outputs.
Phase 2 (Limited Production): enable DPSE for Hosted-only customers who opt-in; expose attestation download in Console under Compliance > Deletions.
Phase 3 (Dedicated/Private): ship Kubernetes operator and onboarding docs; provide enterprise migration runbook and SIEM sink configs.
Phase 4 (GA): default enforcement for configured retention policies and automated attestation exports for enterprise tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a retention policy with region=eu and retention=90d, executing a purge plan removes eligible objects in eu region and emits signed manifests for each batch.
Verification pipeline runs within the scheduled window and produces VerificationSnapshots whose Merkle roots match the ledger; mismatches trigger an incident and create a forensics bundle.
Console surfaces a downloadable attestation bundle containing manifests, verification snapshots, and KMS fingerprints for a selected purge within 24 hours of completion.
Operator supports dry-run and replay modes and passes the retention simulator test suite (integration test coverage >= 85% for purge flows).
Security review signoff and KMS/HSM integration tests complete with keys rotated per policy.

updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Runtime + Infra), Security, and Console. Agreed to use Kafka-based ledger for Hosted and S3-backed compacted store for Private.
2026-03-04: Prototype DeletionManifest schema posted to Confluence (link below). Initial feedback from Security: require KMS signing + proof of key rotation history.
2026-03-06: Eng proposed operator approach; Runtime team raised concern about batch impact on KV cache eviction and suggested integration with autoscaling throttle windows.
2026-03-09: Product review: scoped Phase 1 to Hosted opt-in and dry-run for all tiers; added SIEM sink as an MVP export target.
2026-03-10: PM reviewed cost estimate for big purges; recommending rate-limited default and an opt-in accelerated path for enterprise customers behind a consented SLA.
risks: Large-scale purges could affect serving latency if not properly throttled; mitigation: conservative defaults + autoscaling integration.
On-prem deployments with air-gapped storage may need a different evidence exporter (signed USB bundles); require runbook and manual verification flow.
Cryptographic key compromise would undermine proofs; require KMS/HSM + key rotation policies and emergency revocation procedures.
False positives/negatives in the verifier could create unnecessary incidents; include a confidence scoring and manual-review step within the first 3 months.
